## Open-source solver observations

### Native SCIP with a four-hour allowance

A cold scalar STO/W observation used PySCIPOpt 6.2.1,
SCIP 10.0.2 and SoPlex 8.0.2, with the frozen h215 workbook, nine equiprobable
scenarios and unchanged mathematical/penalty contract. The computational process completed
operationally, but the native solve reached its time limit with **zero solutions**.

| Quantity | Original SCIP observation |
|:--|--:|
| Native ceiling, s | 14,400 |
| Native returned runtime, s | 14,410.76 |
| Construction, s | 249.83 |
| End-to-end, s | 14,939.75 |
| Slurm worker MaxRSS, GiB | 88.90 |
| Usable incumbents | 0 |

: Original scalar SCIP h215 W time-limited observation; operational completion is not solution feasibility. {#tbl-scalar-scip}

No objective, economic subtotal, domestic service or computable native/common
gap is available. The native dual bound was -1.77946e15 BRL; it is retained as a
lower bound, not an economic result. The independent validator rejected the
empty candidate exports. 
The original native matrix had 14,129,174 variables and 810,097 constraints.
The log reports 608.24 seconds of presolve, 12,708,003 presolved variables and
one processed node. These records do not prove root-LP completion.
Native matrix counts reflect backend representation and are not directly
interchangeable with Gurobi linear/general-constraint counts. The four-thread
setting is a ceiling, not evidence of four effective LP/search threads.

Application sampling was sparse: the largest interval was 14,414.81 seconds.
Sampled RSS, Slurm MaxRSS and reported sampler elapsed work have distinct scopes;
the latter is not demonstrated observer CPU overhead or a causal slowdown.
The 192-GiB allocation is retained without inferring a smaller safe envelope.
Historical Gurobi STO/W h215 returned a validated incumbent in 2,445.52 seconds
with 0.740159% gap. Different dates, attained quality, native representations
and uncontrolled shared-system effects preclude a causal solver speedup claim.

This negative observation is separate from the eleven accepted feasible
Gurobi scalar observations and from historical hierarchical SCIP trials.
It documents difficulty under this finite configuration, not general
open-source inability. The original HiGHS attempt ended during worker initialization, without
retained population-solve evidence. It is an operational failure, not a second
numerical no-incumbent observation. Public miniature controls of other interfaces
establish implementation behavior, rather than additional h215 performance
observations.

### Pyomo/APPSI HiGHS with an eight-hour allowance

The HiGHS experiment used the same h215 input, selected warehouse-only network,
nine equiprobable scenarios and effective costs as the Gurobi STO observation.
Pyomo 6.10.1 and HiGHS 1.15.1 were used through APPSI, with four threads,
a 28800-second native allowance and a 1% relative-gap target. Candidate slack
indicators were replaced by the bounded representation proved in Appendix C.
Its equivalence concerns the physical and investment projection and optimal
scalar value, rather than identical redundant slack regions or solver search.

HiGHS returned a feasible solution that passed the original independent
validation, with no failed checks at the stated tolerances. The
[experiment and certificate record](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/ad2ded8132bf5171be65c0113b3d0026c22b2e7b/docs/evidence/scalar_highs_h215_2226536_inspection.json)
retains the source, input, validation and resource identities.
@tbl-highs-h215 compares the returned objective, attained gap and native runtime
with the earlier Gurobi observation.

| Implementation | Objective, BRL trillion | Gap, % | Native runtime, min |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| Native Gurobi | 13.071397 | 0.740159 | 40.76 |
| Pyomo/APPSI HiGHS | 12.974673 | 0.000196 | 426.70 |

: Validated h215 STO/W observations. The inputs and scalar interpretation are
common, but interfaces, redundant-slack representations, attained gaps and
execution dates differ. These are not matched runtime replications. {#tbl-highs-h215}

The smaller HiGHS objective is compatible with the earlier Gurobi bound
interval. It is approximately 0.740% below the earlier incumbent, while both
observations satisfy the 1% criterion. HiGHS's financial subtotal is
393.331 billion BRL, domestic service is 92.3284%, and artificial penalties
account for 96.9685% of its objective. Thus, the near-zero relative gap does
not remove the substantial modeled shortage or establish economic calibration.

The HiGHS model has 14054654 variables, including 307 binaries, 735577 linear
rows and 52217866 nonzeros. Its native log reports one processed node and
2901682 LP iterations. It also records parallel search off with one maximum
worker despite the four-thread setting. These are backend observations;
they do not isolate the cause of runtime. The externally sampled worker-tree
peak is 55.22 GiB. This scope differs from Gurobi's sampled application RSS
and should not be treated as a matched memory-efficiency measurement.

### Interrupted extended SCIP attempt

A further native SCIP attempt used a 28800-second allowance but was
externally terminated before a native terminal report or validated solution
was exported. Its retained completion record is incomplete. The
[forensic record](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/ad2ded8132bf5171be65c0113b3d0026c22b2e7b/docs/evidence/scalar_scip_h215_2226388_inspection.json)
confirms the original input and source identities and a controller-issued
termination signal. The log ends after presolve; it does not establish
root-LP completion, a normally returned time-limit status or an internal
incumbent count. This attempt is therefore censored, rather than another
completed no-incumbent observation.

Taken together, these experiments show configuration-specific computational
difficulty and a successful open-source solution at h215. They support neither
a general impossibility claim for open-source software nor a causal ranking
of solver performance. The earlier HiGHS initialization failure is retained
as an operational record and supplies no numerical performance observation.
